Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Obese adults with depression had significantly lower mean serum 25(OH)D than obese adults without depression.
Sentence: "The mean 25(OH) D levels were significantly different between depressed and non-depressed groups (20 ± 15 vs. 27 ± 13, P < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression (DSM-5 diagnosis)
Population: Obese adults aged 18-60 attending an outpatient obesity clinic in Tehran, Iran, with and without DSM-5 depression
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (observational exposure)
Comparator: Obese adults without depression
Design: case-control study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation at baseline was not associated with depression at 2.5 years in people with multiple sclerosis.
Sentence: "Vitamin D supplementation and meditation were not associated with outcomes."
Measured as: depression
Population: People with multiple sclerosis from the HOLISM study who completed baseline and 2.5-year follow-up surveys
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation (self-reported, assessed at baseline)
Comparator: No vitamin D supplementation
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 1,401
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
